chapter: Working in New York and Europe
title: George Gruntz big band tours and Montreux with Miles and Gil Evans
summary: The Gruntz tours gave steady income, ending with the Montreux concert combining Gruntz and Gil Evans bands; he built a network of European musicians.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: – for me, as an extremely low income freelance crazy kid, that provided some income which for me was wonderful. Because we would do a tour – I was trying to think, because I was thinking about Sheila – we did a tour in ’84, in ’83 and ’84, and ’87, and ’88, and maybe one or two more, and then in ’90 or ’91 I did one more that I was invited to, and that was the one that was with Quincy and Miles at Montreux where they combined forces or the George Gruntz band and the Gil Evans, re-formed Gil Evans band with Gil Goldstein. And that was a great experience. But through that time I would network and I would make friends with musicians in Switzerland, in Holland, in Germany, in Austria. So I would then, a lot of back and forth. A lot of like I’d be in New York, I would play with people in Holland. Come home. Be in New York. Go play with people in Switzerland. Go home. And the Swiss groups were often a mix of like one or two Americans, maybe an Italian or a French, and then three Swiss. So it would be this kind of wonderful wacky mix of free improv and written, difficult written music, and jazz, in lots of different configurations over the years.
